title: Create a new file repos/identity-vessel/src/resolvers/bootstrap-admin.ts implementing a one-time admin-key bootstrap for
description:
Create a new file repos/identity-vessel/src/resolvers/bootstrap-admin.ts implementing a one-time admin-key bootstrap for a substrate whose keyspace has no admin credential.

Export `async function bootstrapAdminKey(c)` (a Hono context handler body helper) returning a result object. It must enforce ALL FOUR of these gates in order, failing closed:

1. LOOPBACK ONLY: use `getConnInfo` from 'hono/bun' to read the real socket peer address. Accept only '127.0.0.1', '::1', or '::ffff:127.0.0.1'. Do NOT trust the x-forwarded-for header — it is spoofable. Reject with 403 BOOTSTRAP_NOT_LOCAL otherwise.
2. CALLER BINDING: require an `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` header. Validate it with `validateKey` from '../services/validation' and reject revoked keys with `isKeyRevoked`. Use the resulting org_id and user_id to bind the minted key. Admin scope is NOT required here — that is the point of the endpoint.
3. IN-CONTAINER PROOF: the JSON body must contain `bootstrap_secret` exactly equal to `process.env.API_KEY_SECRET`. Compare in constant time (equal lengths then XOR accumulate, or crypto.timingSafeEqual over Buffers). Reject with 403 BOOTSTRAP_BAD_SECRET. This proves the caller can read the root-only /etc/substrate/env.
4. ONLY WHEN NO ADMIN EXISTS: query SurrealDB via `const { query } = await import('../db/surrealdb')` for `SELECT scopes, is_active, expires_at FROM api_key WHERE org_id = $org_id;`. If any row is active (is_active true), not expired, and has 'admin' in scopes, refuse with 409 ADMIN_KEY_EXISTS. This makes the endpoint inert on a healthy substrate.

Only when all four pass, mint the key by calling `issueApiKey` from './issue-key' with name 'substrate-admin' and scopes ['read','write','admin'] for the bound org_id/user_id. Because issueApiKey itself calls authorizeAdmin and the caller has no admin credential, bypass that check by calling the underlying key-creation path directly rather than going through authorizeAdmin — read issue-key.ts and reuse its actual minting function.

Log loudly with a '[BootstrapAdmin]' prefix on both success and every refusal, including which gate refused. Never log the minted key or the bootstrap secret.

Write clear comments explaining WHY each gate exists, matching the existing commenting style in this repo (which explains the incident behind a guard). This exists because seed-identity.ts mints substrate-admin only on the genuine first-boot path, so any substrate seeded before that step can never satisfy the SEC-5 admin gate.

Use TypeScript, match the existing code style, and make sure it typechecks.
